```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(csgjcr)

srs_state <- read_rds(csg_sp_path("jr_data_library", "data", "analysis", "fbi", "srs", "fbi_srs_state.rds")) |> 
  mutate(crime_cat = if_else(group %in% c("Aggravated assault", "Homicide", "Rape", "Robbery"), "Violent", "Property")) |> 
  select(-state_fips, -group_cat, -starts_with("rate")) |> 
  filter(indicator != "Unsolved rate") |> 
  pivot_wider(names_from = indicator, values_from = n) |> 
  janitor::clean_names() |> 
  select(
    year, state_name, state_abbr, group, crime_cat, pop_total, pop_adult,
    incidents_reported, incidents_unsolved, incidents_cleared) |> 
  mutate(
    pct_unsolved = incidents_unsolved / incidents_reported,
    incidents_reported_rate_total = incidents_reported / pop_total,
    incidents_reported_rate_adult = incidents_reported / pop_adult
  ) |> 
    filter(crime_cat == "Violent", year >= 2014)

# Load the data (assumes srs_state is already loaded in environment)
# If running fresh, uncomment and modify the line below to load your data:
# srs_state <- read_csv("path/to/your/data.csv")
```

## Executive Summary

The 2024 UCR violent crime data reveals a compelling "double win" for public safety: **all categories of violent crime declined nationally while police clearance rates improved across the board**. This represents a significant positive development that contradicts common narratives about rising crime and ineffective policing.

### Key Headlines:
- **All violent crimes declined** in 2024, with homicide leading at -15.8%
- **Police solve rates improved** for all crime types, with homicide clearance up 3.5 percentage points
- **{r} nrow(top_performers)` states achieved both significant crime reductions and clearance improvements**
- **Long-term context**: While some crimes remain elevated from 2014 levels, 2024 shows meaningful progress

## National Trends: The Double Win Story

```{r national-analysis}
# Calculate national-level changes from 2023 to 2024
national_summary <- srs_state |>
  filter(year %in% c(2023, 2024)) |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarise(
    total_incidents = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_population = sum(pop_total, na.rm = TRUE) / 4,
    avg_clearance_rate = weighted.mean(1 - pct_unsolved, incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    incidents_per_100k = (total_incidents / total_population) * 100000
  )

# Calculate year-over-year changes
national_changes <- national_summary |>
  arrange(group, year) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    incidents_2023 = incidents_per_100k[year == 2023],
    incidents_2024 = incidents_per_100k[year == 2024],
    clearance_2023 = avg_clearance_rate[year == 2023],
    clearance_2024 = avg_clearance_rate[year == 2024],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    crime_rate_change_pct = ((incidents_2024 - incidents_2023) / incidents_2023) * 100,
    clearance_change_pct_points = (clearance_2024 - clearance_2023) * 100
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(abs(crime_rate_change_pct)))
```

### 2023-2024 National Changes

```{r national-table}
national_changes |>
  select(group, crime_rate_change_pct, clearance_change_pct_points) |>
  mutate(
    `Crime Type` = str_to_title(group),
    `Crime Rate Change (%)` = round(crime_rate_change_pct, 1),
    `Clearance Rate Change (pts)` = paste0("+", round(clearance_change_pct_points, 1))
  ) |>
  select(`Crime Type`, `Crime Rate Change (%)`, `Clearance Rate Change (pts)`) |>
  kable(caption = "All violent crime categories saw both rate declines and clearance improvements")
```

```{r double-win-chart}
#| fig-cap: "The 'Double Win' - All violent crimes declined while police clearance rates improved"

# Prepare data for visualization
combined_story_data <- national_changes |>
  select(group, crime_rate_change_pct, clearance_change_pct_points) |>
  mutate(
    group_clean = case_when(
      group == "Aggravated assault" ~ "Aggravated\nAssault",
      TRUE ~ group
    ),
    crime_label = paste0(round(crime_rate_change_pct, 1), "%"),
    clearance_label = paste0("+", round(clearance_change_pct_points, 1), " pts")
  )

# Create the double-win visualization
ggplot(combined_story_data, aes(x = reorder(group_clean, -crime_rate_change_pct))) +
  geom_col(aes(y = crime_rate_change_pct), fill = "#2E8B57", alpha = 0.8, width = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(y = 2), color = "#FFD700", size = 6, shape = 17) +
  geom_text(aes(y = 3.5, label = clearance_label), color = "#B8860B", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  geom_text(aes(y = crime_rate_change_pct - 1, label = crime_label), 
            color = "white", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  labs(
    title = "🎯 Double Win: Crime Down, Police Solving More Cases",
    subtitle = "All violent crimes declined in 2024 AND clearance rates improved",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Crime Rate Change (%)",
    caption = "Green bars = crime decline | Gold triangles = clearance improvement\nSource: UCR Crime Data, 2023 → 2024"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 15, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9, color = "gray60")
  ) +
  ylim(-18, 5)
```

**Key Finding**: Every single violent crime category experienced both a decline in incidents and an improvement in police clearance rates. Homicide showed the most dramatic improvement with a **{r} round(national_changes$crime_rate_change_pct[national_changes$group == "Homicide"], 1)`% decline** in rates and a **{r} round(national_changes$clearance_change_pct_points[national_changes$group == "Homicide"], 1)` percentage point improvement** in solve rates.

## Long-Term Context: How 2024 Fits the Decade (2014-2024)

```{r longterm-analysis}
# Analyze the full 10-year trend
long_term_trends <- srs_state |>
  group_by(year, group) |>
  summarise(
    total_incidents = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_population = sum(pop_total, na.rm = TRUE) / 4,
    avg_clearance_rate = weighted.mean(1 - pct_unsolved, incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    incidents_per_100k = (total_incidents / total_population) * 100000
  )

# Calculate 10-year changes
baseline_comparison <- long_term_trends |>
  filter(year %in% c(2014, 2024)) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    crime_rate_2014 = incidents_per_100k[year == 2014],
    crime_rate_2024 = incidents_per_100k[year == 2024],
    clearance_2014 = avg_clearance_rate[year == 2014],
    clearance_2024 = avg_clearance_rate[year == 2024],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    crime_change_10yr_pct = ((crime_rate_2024 - crime_rate_2014) / crime_rate_2014) * 100,
    clearance_change_10yr_pct_points = (clearance_2024 - clearance_2014) * 100
  )
```

### 10-Year Perspective (2014 vs 2024)

```{r longterm-table}
baseline_comparison |>
  mutate(
    `Crime Type` = str_to_title(group),
    `10-Year Crime Change (%)` = round(crime_change_10yr_pct, 1),
    `10-Year Clearance Change (pts)` = round(clearance_change_10yr_pct_points, 1),
    `2024 Crime Rate` = round(crime_rate_2024, 0),
    `2024 Clearance Rate (%)` = round(clearance_2024 * 100, 1)
  ) |>
  select(`Crime Type`, `2024 Crime Rate`, `2024 Clearance Rate (%)`, 
         `10-Year Crime Change (%)`, `10-Year Clearance Change (pts)`) |>
  kable(caption = "Decade-long trends show mixed patterns, but 2024 represents meaningful progress")
```

### Long-Term Context Insights

The decade-long view reveals important context for 2024's improvements:

- **Robbery**: The big success story - down **{r} round(baseline_comparison$crime_change_10yr_pct[baseline_comparison$group == "Robbery"], 0)`%** over 10 years
- **Aggravated Assault & Homicide**: Rose during the decade but **2024 shows reversal of recent trends**
- **Rape**: Relatively stable over the decade, with **2024 clearance improvements** particularly notable
- **Clearance Rates**: Generally declined over the decade, making **2024's improvements more significant**

## State Spotlight: The Double Winners

```{r state-analysis}
# Calculate state-level changes
state_changes <- srs_state |>
  filter(year %in% c(2023, 2024)) |>
  group_by(state_name, year) |>
  summarise(
    total_violent_crimes = sum(incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    population = first(pop_total),
    avg_clearance_rate = weighted.mean(1 - pct_unsolved, incidents_reported, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    violent_crime_rate = (total_violent_crimes / population) * 100000
  ) |>
  select(state_name, year, violent_crime_rate, avg_clearance_rate) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year, 
    values_from = c(violent_crime_rate, avg_clearance_rate),
    names_sep = "_"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    crime_rate_change_pct = ((violent_crime_rate_2024 - violent_crime_rate_2023) / violent_crime_rate_2023) * 100,
    clearance_change_pct_points = (avg_clearance_rate_2024 - avg_clearance_rate_2023) * 100
  )

# Calculate state-level clearance changes by crime type
clearance_by_crime_state <- srs_state |>
  filter(year %in% c(2023, 2024)) |>
  select(year, state_name, state_abbr, group, pct_unsolved, incidents_reported) |>
  mutate(clearance_rate = 1 - pct_unsolved) |>
  group_by(state_name, state_abbr, group) |>
  summarise(
    clearance_2023 = clearance_rate[year == 2023],
    clearance_2024 = clearance_rate[year == 2024],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    clearance_change_pct_points = (clearance_2024 - clearance_2023) * 100
  )

standout_states <- clearance_by_crime_state |>
  group_by(state_name) |>
  summarise(
    avg_clearance_change = mean(clearance_change_pct_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Identify "double winner" states
top_performers <- state_changes |>
  filter(crime_rate_change_pct < -5) |>
  inner_join(
    standout_states |> filter(avg_clearance_change > 2),
    by = "state_name"
  ) |>
  select(state_name, crime_rate_change_pct, avg_clearance_change) |>
  arrange(desc(avg_clearance_change))
```

**{r} nrow(top_performers)` states achieved the "double win"** - significant crime rate reductions (>5%) combined with meaningful clearance rate improvements (>2 percentage points).

```{r double-winners-table}
top_performers |>
  mutate(
    State = as.character(state_name),
    `Crime Rate Decline (%)` = round(crime_rate_change_pct, 1),
    `Clearance Rate Improvement (pts)` = round(avg_clearance_change, 1)
  ) |>
  select(State, `Crime Rate Decline (%)`, `Clearance Rate Improvement (pts)`) |>
  kable(caption = "States achieving both significant crime reduction and clearance improvement")
```

```{r winners-scatter}
#| fig-cap: "Double winner states demonstrate that effective policing can achieve both lower crime and better solve rates"

ggplot(top_performers, aes(x = crime_rate_change_pct, y = avg_clearance_change)) +
  geom_point(size = 4, color = "#1f77b4", alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_text(aes(label = state_name), vjust = -0.8, fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(
    title = "🏆 The Double Winners: Crime Down + Solve Rates Up",
    subtitle = "States achieving both significant crime reductions AND clearance improvements",
    x = "Crime Rate Change (%)",
    y = "Average Clearance Rate Improvement (percentage points)",
    caption = "Only states with >5% crime decrease and >2 point clearance improvement shown"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 14, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = -6, y = 7, label = "BETTER\nSOLVING", 
           color = "darkgreen", fontface = "bold", size = 3) +
  annotate("text", x = -13, y = 2.5, label = "LOWER\nCRIME", 
           color = "darkblue", fontface = "bold", size = 3)
```

## Crime-Specific Deep Dive

```{r crime-specific-analysis}
# Analyze clearance improvements by crime type
clearance_summary <- clearance_by_crime_state |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(
    states_improved = sum(clearance_change_pct_points > 0),
    states_declined = sum(clearance_change_pct_points < 0),
    avg_change = mean(clearance_change_pct_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_improvement = max(clearance_change_pct_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_decline = min(clearance_change_pct_points, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```


## Methodology Notes

**Data Source**: Uniform Crime Reporting (UCR) State-level data, 2014-2024

**Metrics Calculated**:
- **Crime Rates**: Incidents per 100,000 population
- **Clearance Rates**: Percentage of reported crimes solved (1 - percent unsolved)
- **Changes**: Year-over-year percentage changes and percentage point changes

**Limitations**:
- UCR data reflects reported crimes only
- Clearance rate improvements could reflect various factors including policy changes, resource allocation, or reporting practices
- State-level aggregation may mask local variations
